forces.title: Structural shift towards equity in household savings
forces.description: Indian household portfolios have structurally reallocated towards equities since FY2021, with the proportion of shares and debentures (including mutual funds) rising from 6.6% to 7.6% between pre- and post-pandemic periods. This reflects increasing investor appetite for market-linked returns and a shift away from traditional savings, providing a sustained growth impetus for brokerage and investment services.
forces.source_title: India’s new insurance track: The marathon becomes an AI-led decathlon

forces.title: Rapid growth in demat accounts signals formal market participation
forces.description: Demat accounts in India expanded significantly, growing almost eightfold from 28 million in FY2017 to 225 million by FY2026. This substantial increase indicates a broad-based expansion of formal participation in capital markets. This trend provides a foundational tailwind for brokerage firms by enlarging the investor base and increasing potential trading volumes and investment activity, driving overall market growth.
forces.source_title: India’s new insurance track: The marathon becomes an AI-led decathlon

forces.title: Hardening G-sec yields impact corporate bond issuance
forces.description: Corporate bond issuance through private placements eased in July 2026, dropping to INR 78,063 crore from INR 102,077 crore in June. This deceleration was primarily driven by hardening G-sec yields, which made bond market financing less attractive. Consequently, large corporate borrowers became more reliant on bank credit, reducing opportunities for Debt Capital Markets (DCM) arrangers within investment banking activities.

forces.title: Tokenization to transform capital markets and asset issuance
forces.description: Tokenization of Digital Real-World Assets (RWAs) is poised to unlock a $20 trillion global opportunity by 2030, fundamentally reshaping capital markets. This structural shift offers advantages such as near-instant settlement, enhanced collateral efficiency, global distribution, and fractionalized access. This will create new avenues for investment banking in asset issuance, structuring, and trading platforms for tokenized securities, driving innovation and market expansion.
forces.source_title: Balance: Thriving in the Age of AI

forces.title: Resurgent global fintech M&A fuels investment banking activity
forces.description: Global fintech investment surged to $103.1 billion in H1 2026, driven significantly by M&A activity, which accounted for $67.9 billion. This resurgence, characterized by increased capital deployment and exits in mature, scalable fintechs and digital asset platforms, signals growing investor confidence. This trend directly benefits investment banks through higher deal volumes, advisory fees, and opportunities in structuring complex M&A transactions within the burgeoning fintech sector.

forces.title: Growing UHNWI population boosts demand for sophisticated financial services
forces.description: India's Ultra-High-Net-Worth Individual (UHNWI) population is projected to grow significantly from 19,877 in 2026 to 25,217 by 2031. This expansion is supported by deeper capital markets, digitalization, entrepreneurship, and increasing private capital. A larger UHNWI base drives demand for sophisticated investment banking services, including bespoke advisory, wealth management, private placements, and complex financial structuring, providing a strong tailwind for the sector.

forces.title: SEBI reforms enhance investor protection and market trust
forces.description: India's capital markets have achieved a perfect score of 10 in protecting shareholders' rights, according to the World Bank's Ease of Doing Business 2020 report, a testament to effective reforms by SEBI. This strong regulatory framework fosters greater investor trust and confidence, encouraging broader participation in equity markets. This transparency acts as a tailwind, attracting both domestic and foreign investment, thereby boosting activity for brokerages and investment banks.

forces.title: India's rising global market cap ranking boosts equity appeal
forces.description: India's climb to the fifth position in global market capitalization rankings by June 2025, holding a 4% share, signifies increasing investor faith and the resilience of Indian equities on a global scale. This enhanced international standing makes Indian markets more attractive to foreign portfolio investors and institutional capital, acting as a tailwind by potentially increasing foreign investment inflows and overall market liquidity, benefiting investment banking and brokerage.

forces.title: Rising incomes drive broader demand for financial services
forces.description: Rising disposable incomes across all income brackets in India are fueling a broader demand for financial services. As individuals accumulate more wealth, their propensity to invest in capital market products, seek financial advice, and participate in organized savings schemes increases. This fundamental economic trend serves as a strong tailwind, expanding the potential client base and asset pools for brokerage firms and investment banks.

viewpoints.title: India's IPO market sees record fundraising and strong pipeline ahead
viewpoints.description: IBEF reports record IPO fundraising in 2025, reaching approximately INR 1.95 lakh crore (USD 22.55 billion) across 365 IPOs, with December 2025 mobilisation at INR 1.76 lakh crore (USD 20.35 billion). This marks consecutive highs, indicating strong investor confidence. A robust pipeline of over INR 4 lakh crore (USD 45.5 billion) is projected for 2026, signaling sustained activity and significant deal flow for investment banks and IPO managers.

viewpoints.title: Global fintech M&A investment shows renewed vigor and investor confidence
viewpoints.description: KPMG reports global fintech investment reached $103.1 billion in H1 2026, on track for a four-year high, with M&A comprising the largest share at $67.9 billion. This resurgence of capital deployed and exits, despite soft deal volumes, signals growing investor confidence, particularly in scalable platforms involving digital assets and AI. This trend is highly favorable for investment banks engaged in M&A advisory services.

viewpoints.title: Indian equity market sees unprecedented household participation and wealth creation
viewpoints.description: IBEF highlights the Indian equity market's rapid growth, with one-fifth of households now connected to stock markets and market capitalization increasing sixfold over the decade. A record 2.32 crore new investors in 2024 and over 21 crore stock market-linked accounts underscore expanding direct equity engagement. This surge in participation has generated substantial household wealth, indicating strong retail investor confidence and activity for brokerage services.
